home.title: Psychological support for children and families
home.intro: Sometimes, a child's behaviour is the visible part of emotions that are hard to express, developmental needs, or difficulties in their relationships. Together, we can better understand what lies behind these expressions and find support suited to the child, the parent, their relationship, and the whole family.
home.recognitionTitle: You may have come here because…
recognition: your child is going through a difficult time and you want to understand their experience better;
you notice emotional, behavioural, or relational changes that concern you;
your relationship with your child has become strained, or understanding each other feels harder;
your child finds it difficult to adjust to nursery, school, or other changes in their life;
tensions between siblings or other difficulties affect the balance of the whole family;
the challenges of parenting feel overwhelming and you need support to understand your child's needs and how to be there for them.

supports.title: Your child
supports.text: When you notice emotional, behavioural, relational, or adjustment difficulties and want to better understand the needs behind them.

supports.title: You, as a parent
supports.text: When you need support to understand your child's experience, respond to their needs, and feel more confident as a parent.

supports.title: Family relationships
supports.text: When tensions arise between parent and child, between siblings, or within the family, and you need support to understand them and build more balanced relationships.

supports.title: Online support for Romanians abroad
supports.text: Psychological support sessions in Romanian, held exclusively online, for children, parents, and families living outside Romania.

home.approachTitle: First, we understand. Then, we build together.
home.approachText: In my work, professional training and clinical experience meet a calm, authentic, and approachable presence. I want the people I work with to feel heard, respected, and understood, without judgement or pressure to find every answer immediately.
steps: Send an inquiry, even if you do not yet know which form of support is appropriate.
We discuss the request and clarify the child's and family's needs.
We agree on a next step when working together is appropriate.
home.resourcesIntro: Articles about child development, parenting, and family relationships.
home.closingTitle: You do not need to have every answer.
home.closingText: You can start with a question. Together, we can clarify what kind of support might be appropriate.

services.title: Forms of support
services.intro: The child, parent, and family relationships are considered together, in the context of development and experience. Explore the areas below or contact me if you are unsure what would be appropriate.
services.initial: During first contact, we clarify the request and discuss support appropriate to your circumstances.

items.title: Clinical psychological assessment
items.text: Assessment helps understand a child's or adolescent's emotional, behavioural, and relational functioning in the context of their development.
examples: Understanding the difficulties observed and the child's needs.
Clarifying possible directions for support and intervention.

items.title: Counselling for children and adolescents
items.text: Support adapted to a child's or adolescent's age and needs, in relation to everyday challenges.
examples: Changes in the family, at school, or in important relationships.

items.title: Integrative psychotherapy for children and adolescents
items.text: Relational integrative work considers the child within their story, development, and relationships. Goals and ways of working are developed collaboratively with the family.
examples: Understanding experiences and developing emotional resources.
Supporting relationships and more adaptive ways of meeting challenges.

items.title: Parent counselling
items.text: A space for reflection and support that considers the child's needs alongside the adult's resources, limits, and experiences.
examples: Understanding a child's behaviour and its context.

items.title: The parent–child relationship
items.text: Support to understand and improve the relationship between parent and child, with attention to each person's needs and perspective.
examples: Building more balanced ways of relating.

items.title: Family dynamics and relationships
items.text: We consider how relationships and changes within the family affect each member, without reducing difficulties to one person.
examples: Relationships between siblings and between children and caregivers.
Changes or tensions affecting the family's balance.

items.title: Online support for Romanians abroad
items.text: Psychological support sessions in Romanian, held exclusively online, for children, parents, and families living outside Romania.
examples: Suitability for online work is discussed individually.
Availability and arrangements are clarified before an appointment.

about.title: About me
about.valuesTitle: The values that guide my work

values.title: Relationship
values.text: Change begins and develops in safe, stable, authentic relationships.

values.title: Respect
values.text: I respect the pace, uniqueness, limits, and story of each person and family.

values.title: Professional ethics
values.text: I work responsibly, within clear professional boundaries, using scientifically grounded interventions.

values.title: Authenticity
values.text: I believe in a human, natural, sincere professional presence, without constructing an image of a ‘perfect’ professional.

values.title: Balance
values.text: I seek balance between emotion and reason, children's and parents' needs, acceptance and change, and professional and personal life.

resources.title: Resources for children, parents, and families
resources.intro: Perspectives and information to understand child development and family relationships. These materials are informative and do not replace an individual assessment or support.
resources.emptyText: Try another word or return to all topics.
resources.notice: General information does not establish a diagnosis or replace a discussion of your circumstances.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.intro: Answers that may help before first contact. You can send an inquiry about questions specific to your circumstances.

items.question: Do I need to know which service I need?
items.answer: No. You can choose ‘I'm not sure’ in the form. First contact helps clarify the request and discuss which direction of support may be appropriate.

items.question: Does submitting the form book an appointment?
items.answer: No. The form sends an inquiry. An appointment and working arrangements are agreed separately after discussing the request.

items.question: What should I include in the message?
items.answer: A brief message is enough, and the field is optional. For this first contact, avoid medical details and sensitive information about you or your child.

items.question: Are parents involved?
items.answer: Collaboration with parents is an important part of the process. Their involvement is adapted to the child's age, needs, and the goals agreed together.

items.question: How is the form of support chosen?
items.answer: The process begins with understanding the situation and clarifying needs. On this basis, we discuss goals and appropriate support within professional competencies.

items.question: How long does the work take?
items.answer: Duration varies with needs, goals, and progress. The website does not set a universal duration; arrangements and review of goals are discussed together.

items.question: Can I ask for support if I live outside Romania?
items.answer: You can ask about online support in Romanian. Suitability, whether working together is possible, and applicable arrangements are discussed individually before an appointment.

items.question: Are sessions available in every website language?
items.answer: The languages available on the website do not automatically indicate the languages in which sessions are provided. Please ask for clarification before an appointment.

items.question: How is confidentiality approached?
items.answer: Confidentiality and its limits are discussed within the working relationship, in line with applicable professional and legal obligations. It is not a promise without exceptions; you can ask about specific questions.

legal.draftNotice: Prepared for review. Information marked “TO CONFIRM” and provider practices must be validated before publication.

privacySections.title: Who is responsible for your data
privacySections.text: Cabinet Individual Psihologie - Stănculea Maria Valeria is the controller of data used in the practice. Contact: psiholog.mariavaleriabaciu@gmail.com. Tax identifier: [TO CONFIRM]. Registered/professional address: [TO CONFIRM]. Practice registration and professional code: [TO CONFIRM]. Authorised persons with access and, if appointed, the data protection officer’s contact: [TO CONFIRM].

privacySections.title: Data we need
privacySections.text: The form asks for your name, email and enquiry category; the message is optional. The page language and selected service, if any, are also sent. Name and email are needed to reply through the form. It does not request files, national identifiers, diagnoses or bank details. The category and message may indirectly reveal health information: avoid clinical details and other people’s data at first contact. Providers may process IP addresses, browser information and technical logs.

privacySections.title: Purposes and legal bases
privacySections.text: Steps you request before a contract and performance of the contract: GDPR Article 6(1)(b). General questions and abuse prevention: legitimate interests under Article 6(1)(f), subject to an assessment of necessity and your rights [TO CONFIRM]. Applicable legal obligations: Article 6(1)(c). Form data is not used for marketing. Acknowledging this notice is not blanket consent to all processing.

privacySections.title: Clinical data and professional confidentiality
privacySections.text: Before services begin, you receive specific information about assessment, counselling or psychotherapy and the scope and limits of confidentiality. Health data also requires an Article 9 condition: for healthcare, Article 9(2)(h) together with Article 9(3), where the legal and professional secrecy conditions are met. Bases for each activity and any other purpose: [TO CONFIRM]. Professional informed consent, GDPR consent and consent to cookies serve different purposes.

privacySections.title: Children and adolescents
privacySections.text: For an initial enquiry, use a parent’s or legal representative’s contact details and avoid identifying the child or providing medical history in the form. Representation and required permissions are checked before services. The Romanian professional code requires both parents’ consent to counselling and psychotherapy where parental authority is shared, subject to applicable legal exceptions. Information for the child is adapted to their age and understanding.

privacySections.title: Recipients and providers
privacySections.text: EmailJS sends the enquiry through the connected Gmail service to the practice. EmailJS history is configured to retain the name, email, message and enquiry parameters; Analytics is disabled. Gmail retains the received email. GitHub Pages hosts the site and may process technical data. Google provides abuse prevention. Authorised persons, the Gmail account type, processing agreements and the online consultation platform: [TO CONFIRM]. Disclosure to authorities takes place only as permitted or required by law.

privacySections.title: reCAPTCHA verification
privacySections.text: Google reCAPTCHA v2 loads automatically on Contact. It uses technical signals to prevent abuse and may set cookies. Google states that, since 2 April 2026, it acts as processor for this data under Google Cloud terms. The form does not pass your message as a reCAPTCHA analysis parameter. The necessity of automatic loading and cookie lifetimes are [TO CONFIRM]. Direct email remains available.

privacySections.title: Processing outside the EEA
privacySections.text: EmailJS declares processing in the USA and standard contractual clauses for EU transfers. GitHub, Google and email providers may involve processing outside the European Economic Area. Contracting entities, locations, safeguards and the assessment of the practice’s actual transfers: [TO CONFIRM]. You may request information and a copy of applicable safeguards by email. A provider’s public policy does not verify the practice’s account configuration.

privacySections.title: Retention
privacySections.text: Proposed rule for Gmail enquiries without a contract: six months after the last interaction, followed by periodic deletion. EmailJS declares 30 days for active-account data; its application to this account’s history and existing copies needs verification. Deletion procedures: [TO CONFIRM]. Psychological tests, results, professional notes and recordings must be retained for at least ten years after the professional relationship ends under point 42 of the Romanian professional code, or longer where required by law. Contract, tax, dispute and backup retention periods: [TO CONFIRM], separately from initial enquiries.

privacySections.title: Form data in your browser
privacySections.text: The draft and acknowledgement remain in application memory during internal navigation and disappear on reload. Provider acceptance clears personal fields. The reCAPTCHA token is consumed at every attempt and cleared on expiry or navigation; it is not stored in browser storage or the email. The display preference may be stored locally. The form does not archive or provide durable evidence of clinical consent.

privacySections.title: Your rights
privacySections.text: Under the conditions of GDPR, you may request access, correction, erasure, restriction, portability and object to processing. Where consent is the basis, you may withdraw it without affecting earlier processing. Erasure is not absolute: some records must be kept for professional or legal obligations or legal claims. Requests are assessed against the relevant data and legal basis. Contact does not require marketing consent.

privacySections.title: Exercising your rights
privacySections.text: Email the practice. Responses are normally free and provided within one month; complex or numerous requests may require two additional months, with reasons and notice within the first month. Where there are reasonable doubts, only information needed to verify identity is requested. You can complain to ANSPDCP or seek a judicial remedy. Contacting the practice first does not remove those rights.

privacySections.title: Security and automated decisions
privacySections.text: We use secure website and provider connections, but email and the internet cannot offer absolute confidentiality. The practice’s access controls, backups and incident procedures: [TO CONFIRM]. The website does not automatically make diagnoses, therapy admission decisions or contracts. reCAPTCHA may technically block sending; direct email is an alternative. Incidents must be managed and notified where GDPR requires.

privacySections.title: Scope and updates
privacySections.text: This notice covers the website and the practice’s general framework. You receive completed information about the particular service, online platform and clinical data before processing begins. Relevant changes are communicated before new purposes or technologies are introduced; an updated text does not retroactively authorise other processing. Items awaiting confirmation are not verified practices.

cookieSections.title: Cookies and similar technologies
cookieSections.text: Cookies and local storage can keep information on your device. This policy covers the application and embedded third-party components; providers’ settings may have separate effects. A technical inventory on the public domain, including each third-party cookie’s name, domain and lifetime: [TO CONFIRM].

cookieSections.title: Display preference
cookieSections.text: The localStorage key “lovable-ui-theme” stores light, dark or system mode. It serves the appearance you request, not advertising, and contains no form data. The application sets no automatic expiry: it remains until you change the option or clear browser data. The website remains usable if storage is blocked.

cookieSections.title: Language, draft and verification
cookieSections.text: The page address determines language without a language cookie. The draft and notice acknowledgement remain only in application memory. The reCAPTCHA token is temporary, consumed on an attempt and cleared on expiry or navigation. The form does not save this information in localStorage.

cookieSections.title: Google reCAPTCHA on Contact
cookieSections.text: Verification v2 loads automatically only on Contact. Google describes “_GRECAPTCHA” as a risk-analysis cookie and technical data processing for security. Actual domains and lifetimes, and access to other Google cookies already in the browser: [TO CONFIRM] through an audit. Your form message is not a reCAPTCHA parameter. Direct email is available.

cookieSections.title: Information, necessity and consent
cookieSections.text: Romanian Law 506/2004, Article 4(5), requires information and consent for storage/access on a device, subject to the limited Article 4(6) exceptions, including strict necessity for a requested service. A “security” label alone does not establish the exception. The assessment of automatic reCAPTCHA loading is [TO CONFIRM]. Any nonessential technology identified by the audit must be blocked until consent, with equally easy refusal and withdrawal. Browsing alone is not consent.

cookieSections.title: Analytics and advertising
cookieSections.text: The application does not load Google Analytics, advertising pixels or marketing tools. EmailJS Analytics is disabled. Provider-side enquiry history is personal data processing described in the GDPR notice, not proof of an analytics cookie on the website. New tools require an assessment and updated information.

cookieSections.title: Controlling storage
cookieSections.text: You can change the display mode and delete or block site data in your browser. Google cookies may belong to another domain and need separate management. Blocking the security component may prevent form submission; you can email directly. Clearing browser data does not delete messages already sent to the practice or EmailJS history.

cookieSections.title: Controller and updates
cookieSections.text: Cabinet Individual Psihologie - Stănculea Maria Valeria is responsible for selecting website technologies. Questions: psiholog.mariavaleriabaciu@gmail.com. The inventory, necessity assessment and provider agreements must be validated before publication. The review date records editorial review, not certification of every cookie in your browser.

termsSections.title: Service provider
termsSections.text: Cabinet Individual Psihologie - Stănculea Maria Valeria presents clinical psychology and relational integrative psychotherapy within authorised professional competence. The professional framework includes Romanian Law 213/2004 and the professional code. Tax identifier, professional address, registration and professional code: [TO CONFIRM]. Contact: psiholog.mariavaleriabaciu@gmail.com. Actual authorisations and specialities must be confirmed before publication.

termsSections.title: Website information
termsSections.text: Materials provide general information and do not replace an individual assessment or advice from a professional familiar with your circumstances. Clinical outcomes or appointment availability are not guaranteed. Service descriptions alone do not constitute a complete contractual offer. Conditions suitable for your enquiry are discussed before collaboration.

termsSections.title: Initial enquiries
termsSections.text: The form starts an enquiry; it does not conclude a contract, book a session or take payment. Technical acceptance does not prove arrival in the inbox. Name and email are necessary for a reply; the message is optional. Avoid clinical information and identifiable details about children. If abuse verification fails, use direct email.

termsSections.title: Email contract and bank transfer
termsSections.text: The contract is sent and concluded by email, with payment made separately by bank transfer according to the practice’s instructions. The website has no checkout or card processing. Before acceptance you receive the agreed service, complete provider identity, total fee and applicable tax treatment, duration/frequency, payment method and rescheduling, cancellation and termination rules. The actual contract and these rules: [TO CONFIRM].

termsSections.title: Online consultations
termsSections.text: Online consultations are available where suitable for the situation and the practice’s competence. The platform, technical requirements, confidentiality conditions and connection-failure procedure are explained before the session; platform: [TO CONFIRM]. A private space and suitable participation conditions are needed. Any audio/video recording requires prior permission and information about purpose and retention; reading the website notice does not provide that permission.

termsSections.title: Professional consent and minors
termsSections.text: Informed consent is obtained before services, including online, following an explanation of purpose, confidentiality limits, benefits, risks, alternatives and fees. Counselling/psychotherapy for minors under shared parental authority requires both parents’ consent, subject to applicable legal exceptions. Representation and information for the child are handled separately. Acknowledging the GDPR notice is not consent to therapy.

termsSections.title: Rescheduling, cancellation and withdrawal
termsSections.text: Request changes by email. Deadlines and any costs are specified in the contract before acceptance; this page creates no penalties. The legal withdrawal regime depends on the actual service: certain healthcare services are excluded from Romanian Emergency Ordinance 34/2014, but not every psychological service is automatically excluded. Where it applies, mandatory information and rights are explained before contracting. Payment alone does not waive a statutory right.

termsSections.title: Emergencies
termsSections.text: The form and email are not emergency channels and should not be assumed to be continuously monitored. For immediate danger to yourself or another person, call 112 in Romania or the local emergency service abroad. An individual crisis-support plan is discussed within the professional relationship.

termsSections.title: Responsible use and content
termsSections.text: You may read materials and share links, respecting copyright and legal exceptions. Do not use the form for spam, unauthorised access or illegal content. Maintenance or providers may affect technical availability. These conditions do not exclude liability or rights that cannot legally be waived.

termsSections.title: Personal data
termsSections.text: The GDPR and cookie policies describe initial enquiries, providers and abuse prevention. Specific clinical-service information is completed separately before processing. Reading the notice does not authorise marketing, session recording or every use of health data. Do not send sensitive data through a channel that has not been agreed for that purpose.

termsSections.title: Questions and disputes
termsSections.text: You may complain to the practice by email without losing the right to contact the competent authority or court. Professional issues may be referred to the Romanian College of Psychologists, and data issues to ANSPDCP. The SAL banner leads to the ANPC platform; admissibility depends on the service and jurisdiction, including healthcare exclusions in Romanian Ordinance 38/2015. The European ODR platform closed in 2025.

termsSections.title: Applicable law and changes
termsSections.text: Romanian law and relevant European rules apply, preserving mandatory protections for service users. The website imposes no exclusive court or waiver of rights. Updates apply to future use and do not retroactively change an existing contract. Complete identity and the actual contract must be reviewed before publication and the first collaboration.
